newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit rises to 162.7 bln levs.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit rises to 162.7 bln levs.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 7.3 billion levs to 162.7 billion levs between November 30 and December 17, or around 79 percent of the revised annual target, Finance Ministry figures showed.
BULGARIA BUDGET DEFICIT, bln levs DEC 17 NOV 30
Note: (R) marks percentage of annual spending and deficit targets assumed in the second budget revisison.

Two weeks ago Bulgaria's parliament passed a revision of this year's budget, raising the spending target to 564.238 billion levs from 438.932 billion to help cover a 125.3 billion lev gap in interest payments on domestic debt.
The largest part of the increase is to be funded through a 15-year 115-billion lev loan from the central bank despite its strong opposition.
The deficit target was raised respectively to 206 billion levs or five to six percent of GDP from 80.715 billion levs. The revenue target was not revised.
The revision, this year's second, was sought by the socialist government after it overshot the macroeconomic targets in the July revision.
Domestic debt rose to 839.3 billion levs at the end of November from 345.4 billion levs at the beginning of the year.
The sharp fall in the lev also boosted the deficit because it increased the volume of lev needed for foreign debt payments.
The lev slumped from 70 to the dollar at the beginning of the year to 487-489 on Friday.
